key_insight: A digitally controlled power converter can improve efficiency by adapting both inductor configuration and switching frequency to the current load instead of using one fixed design point.
engineering_relevance: This enables more efficient integrated power delivery for dynamic workloads by jointly reducing conduction and switching losses while respecting current ripple and CCM constraints.
method: Built an end-to-end workflow combining analytical modeling, FEM simulations, and optimization to choose operating points across load conditions.
Generated a lookup table of preferred inductance-frequency settings and applied them in real time with low-overhead digital control.
Added a hysteresis-based strategy and entry-margin condition to avoid temporary CCM violations during fast load transients.
evidence_signal: Simulations reported a 4.5 percentage-point increase in average efficiency and up to a 32% reduction in average power loss versus fixed configurations.
watch_item: Real-world performance depends on accurate sensing and controller latency, since delayed adaptation can briefly violate CCM during rapid load changes.
paper_title: Adaptive Inductor and Frequency Management for Integrated Power Converters
